title: Build a security group and instances from data files
scenario:
The security team of your organization keeps the firewall rules of the `orders` web tier in `rules.yaml`. They review and change that file, not Terraform code. The platform team wants a configuration in `/home/coder/lab` that builds the security group `orders-web` and the web tier instances from that file and from `terraform.tfvars`, and publishes a few lists other teams consume.

The instances run in the default VPC of the account. Hard-coded AMI, VPC or subnet IDs are not allowed: they differ between accounts.

The folder is initialized. Nothing has been applied yet. The `aws` CLI is configured for the account and region `us-east-1`.

tasks.text:
Create the security group described in `rules.yaml`, with one ingress rule per entry of `rules`.

- Read the file with `yamldecode(file("${path.module}/rules.yaml"))` into a local value.
- `aws_security_group.web` takes its name and description from `security_group` in the file and lives in the default VPC. Look the VPC up with `data "aws_vpc" "default" { default = true }`.
- `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.this` uses `for_each` over the rules, keyed by the rule `name` (for example `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.this["ssh"]`). Map `port`, `protocol` and `cidr` to `from_port`/`to_port`, `ip_protocol` and `cidr_ipv4`.
- Do not change `rules.yaml`.

Hint: a [`for` expression](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/expressions/for) like `{ for r in local.rules : r.name => r }` turns the list into a map for [`for_each`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/meta-arguments/for_each). See the [ingress rule resource](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/resources/vpc_security_group_ingress_rule).
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-security-group-rules --filters Name=group-id,Values=<sg-id>`. The group `orders-web` should have exactly the four ingress rules from `rules.yaml`, and `terraform state list` should show them keyed by name.

tasks.text:
Create one EC2 instance per entry of `var.instances` (declared in `variables.tf`, set in `terraform.tfvars`).

- Use `aws_instance.app` with `for_each = var.instances`.
- The AMI comes from an `aws_ami` data source: owner `amazon`, the most recent image whose name matches `amzn2-ami-hvm-*-x86_64-gp2`.
- The subnet comes from an `aws_subnets` data source filtered on the default VPC (`vpc-id`). Use `sort(data.aws_subnets.default.ids)[each.value.subnet_index]`.
- Attach `aws_security_group.web`. Tag each instance with `Name = <map key>` plus its own `tags`. Use `merge()`.
- Apply the configuration.

Hint: the `optional()` attributes in `variables.tf` already supply defaults (`t3.micro`, subnet index `0`). See [optional object attributes](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/expressions/type-constraints#optional-object-type-attributes).
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=web-1,web-2,batch`. The three instances should run with the expected instance type, subnet and tags.

tasks.text:
Add two outputs and apply.

- `public_tcp_ports`: the distinct, sorted list of ports of the TCP rules that are open to `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `private_ips`: a map of instance name (the `var.instances` key) to its private IP address.

Hint: filter with `[for r in local.rules : r.port if r.protocol == "tcp" && r.cidr == "0.0.0.0/0"]`, then wrap the result in `sort(distinct(...))`. See [collection functions](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/functions/distinct).
tasks.validation: Run `terraform output -json`. `public_tcp_ports` should list 443 and 8443, and `private_ips` should map `web-1`, `web-2` and `batch` to their private IPs.

tasks.text:
`terraform plan` fails in the lab folder. Fix the configuration.

- The platform standard is AWS provider 5.x, the version recorded in `.terraform.lock.hcl`.
- Do not downgrade the provider.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan`. It should run without errors, and `.terraform.lock.hcl` should still select AWS provider 5.x.

tasks.text:
Build the security group from `rules.yaml`.

- `aws_security_group.web` takes its name and description from the file and lives in the default VPC, found with a data source.
- Create one `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.this` per rule and CIDR, keyed `"<name>-<cidr>"` (for example `this["ssh-10.0.0.0/8"]`).
- IPv6 CIDRs (containing `:`) go to `cidr_ipv6`, all others to `cidr_ipv4`.
- The group must have no other ingress rules. Do not change `rules.yaml`.
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-security-group-rules --filters Name=group-id,Values=<sg-id>`. `orders-web` should have one ingress rule per rule and CIDR in `rules.yaml`.

tasks.text:
Create the instances in `terraform.tfvars` as `aws_instance.app` with `for_each`.

- Declare `var.instances` as a `map(object({...}))` with optional attributes: `instance_type` (default `t3.micro`), `subnet_index` (default `0`), `role` (default `worker`) and `tags` (default `{}`). Do not change `terraform.tfvars`.
- AMI: most recent Amazon image matching `amzn2-ami-hvm-*-x86_64-gp2`, from a data source.
- Subnet: element `subnet_index` of the sorted subnet IDs of the default VPC, from an `aws_subnets` data source.
- Attach `aws_security_group.web`. Tags: `Name = <key>`, `Role = <role>`, plus the instance's own `tags`.
- No hard-coded AMI, VPC or subnet IDs.
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=web-1,web-2,batch`. Each instance should have the expected type, subnet, security group and tags.

tasks.text:
Publish these outputs and apply.

- `public_tcp_ports`: distinct ports of the TCP rules open to `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`, in ascending order.
- `private_ips`: map of instance name to private IP.
- `web_instance_ids`: list of the IDs of the instances with `role = web`, ordered by instance name.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform output -json`. `public_tcp_ports` should be `[443, 8443]`, and the other two outputs should match the instances.

tasks.text:
The configuration does not work with the Terraform and provider versions installed in this environment. Fix it.

- Terraform must accept any 1.6.x CLI release.
- The AWS provider must stay on the 5.x version in `.terraform.lock.hcl`.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform version` and `terraform plan`. The plan should run without errors, using AWS provider 5.x.

tasks.text:
Build the security group `orders-web` from both `rules.yaml` and the partner team's `partner-rules.csv`.

- `aws_security_group.web` takes its name and description from `rules.yaml` and lives in the default VPC.
- One `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.this` per rule and CIDR from both files, keyed `"<name>-<cidr>"`. A rule that appears in both files is created once.
- In `rules.yaml`, `protocol` defaults to `tcp`, `to_port` defaults to `port`, and rules with `enabled: false` are skipped.
- IPv6 CIDRs go to `cidr_ipv6`. Do not change the data files.
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-security-group-rules --filters Name=group-id,Values=<sg-id>`. `orders-web` should have exactly one ingress rule per enabled rule and CIDR from both files.

tasks.text:
Create the instances in `terraform.tfvars` as `aws_instance.app`.

- Declare `var.instances` with optional attributes `instance_type` (`t3.micro`), `subnet_index` (`0`), `role` (`worker`), `enabled` (`true`) and `tags` (`{}`). Do not change `terraform.tfvars`.
- Disabled instances must not be created. Keys are the map keys.
- AMI from a data source (most recent Amazon `amzn2-ami-hvm-*-x86_64-gp2`). Subnet: index `subnet_index` of the sorted default-VPC subnet IDs; indexes beyond the end wrap around.
- Attach `aws_security_group.web`. Tags: `Name = <key>`, `Role = <role>`, plus the instance's own `tags`. No hard-coded IDs.
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=web-1,web-2,batch,old`. Only `web-1`, `web-2` and `batch` should exist, each in the expected subnet.

tasks.text:
Publish these outputs and apply.

- `public_tcp_ports`: distinct ports (`from_port`) of the TCP rules open to `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`, as numbers in ascending numeric order.
- `admin_cidrs`: sorted, distinct CIDRs of all rules whose port range includes 22.
- `private_ips`: map of instance name to private IP.
- `instances_by_role`: map of role to the sorted list of instance names with that role.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform output -json`. `public_tcp_ports` should be `[80, 443, 8080]`, and the other outputs should match the rules and instances.
